items.text:
I was a mid-level professional, confident in my skills, and I was absolutely terrified.

I had just started a new job.

On paper, I was qualified.

I had the experience.�  I had the track record.�  I knew what I was doing.

And my stomach was still in knots.

That experience taught me something about confidence that I've never forgotten:

"A big part of being confident is being brave. And you can't be brave unless you're scared."

Experience doesn't make you immune to fear.

A new job, a bigger role, a different industry, more responsibility, any of it can make you quietly wonder:

Can I really do this?

What experience gives you isn't the absence of fear.

It gives you evidence.

Evidence that you've walked into unfamiliar rooms before.�

Evidence that you've figured things out.�  Evidence that you've survived the days when you didn't have all the answers.

So I didn't need to trust the process.

I needed to trust myself.

And I did.

If you're starting a new chapter and you're a little scared, don't 
automatically mistake that feeling for a lack of confidence.

Sometimes you're simply standing at the edge of something you haven't done yet.

#CareerGrowth #Leadership #ProfessionalGrowth #SelfTrust

items.text: I have some credentialing projects coming up and could use some assistance.

🚨 Ready to see patients, but not getting paid? That's the reality many providers face due to credentialing delays.

Credentialing delays are becoming a bigger challenge than ever.

Many insurance carriers are taking months to complete credentialing applications, leaving providers unable to bill for services despite being fully licensed and ready to practice.

A few ways to help prevent delays:
✔️ Keep your CAQH profile updated
 ✔️ Ensure provider information is consistent across all applications
 ✔️ Start the credentialing process well before a provider's start date
 ✔️ Follow up regularly with insurance carriers

At NIHC Group, we help healthcare providers navigate the credentialing process so they can focus on patient care while we handle the details.
